$comment: The single source for everything that occurs more than once on the
site: links, email, photos, meta values. Takes effect immediately —
there is no build. One-off prose deliberately does NOT live here but as
HTML in sections/*.php — there it reads as text, here it would just be
ballast. The values themselves are website content and stay German.
$comment_url: Once the domain is settled: enter it here, e.g. "https://sturmfrei-impro.de"
(without a trailing slash). og:url, canonical, the absolute URLs in the
JSON-LD as well as /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml then follow from it
automatically. While the value is null, those stay away — half an
$comment_ogImage: Path to a 1200x630 image, e.g. "images/og.jpg". Only emitted if "url"
is set as well — social networks need absolute URLs. Without an image,
twitter:card stays on "summary", because a large empty card looks worse
than a small one without an image.

$comment_nav: Label and target of the navigation — once here, not once each in the
header bar and the footer. "page" is the folder name of the page;
"index" is the home page. The footer shows every item, the header bar
the ones with "inHeader": true. The page has to exist in pages()
Home deliberately does not appear in the header bar: the wordmark on
the left is the way back, an extra item would be the same link twice.
"inFooter": false keeps an item out of the footer, and "Kontakt" is
the one that uses it. There is no /kontakt/ page any more — the address
and the number stand in the Impressum, so that is where the item
points. In the header that is the word people look for; in the footer
the same page already stands under its own name among the mandatory
pages a few lines below, and "Kontakt" beside it would be one page
under two names in one list.
$comment_legalNav: The mandatory pages. They live at the bottom of the footer, not in the
header bar — down there they are where people expect them and they take
no space from the main navigation.
$comment_links: Every channel off the site — once here, not once per place it turns up.
The order counts: the follow cards, the footer list and "sameAs" in the
JSON-LD all follow it. A channel added here shows up in all three without
"icon" names a file in public/images/icons/, without the .svg. The glyph
is written into the page instead of linked, so it takes the colour around
it; "brand" is the platform's own colour, and the glyph on the follow
card is what carries it. Both are optional — without an icon the card
stays text, without a brand colour the glyph takes the accent. A new
channel needs a new glyph: a 24x24 SVG next to the others, stroked in
currentColor. A name pointing at no file is reported by `make check`.
"roles" is what the pages ask for, and the reason not one of them names
a platform: "tickets" is the shop a date without a ticket link of its
own falls back to, "announcements" the channel the follow cards offer,
that the button in the teaser for the next date points at and that the
sentence in sections/follow.php names. Move a role to another channel and
every page follows. Each of the two belongs to exactly one channel —
`make check` reports it missing as well as held twice.

$comment_crossfade: The order of the crossfade is not written down here any more. It is
the contents of public/images/group/, sorted the way a person numbers
files, with "hero.photo" moved to the end so the section does not
open with the picture at the top of the page — crossfade_photos() in
lib/data.php. The list stood here as five paths while the folder held
six: one photo the site never showed. Drop a picture into the folder
and it is in the rotation.
photoAlt: what is in the pictures, which a folder cannot say. One
sentence for all of them — they show the same people.
